rules.title: Broker fee paid only by the party that hired the broker
rules.requirement: In Massachusetts, a rental broker's fee may be charged only to the party (landlord or tenant) who first hired the broker under a contract. If the landlord or the landlord's agent hired the broker, the tenant cannot be made to pay the broker fee.
rules.key_value: Broker fee paid only by the party that engaged the broker
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rentals in Massachusetts where a licensed real estate broker or salesperson is used to find a tenant or a rental unit.
rules.citation: M.G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43)
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

notes: The document contains two versions of the section: the text in effect until 2025-08-01 and the text amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43, in effect from 2025-08-01. I made one record from the amended version, the broker-fee payment rule. I did not make a separate record for the licensing requirement ("no person shall engage in the business of finding dwelling accommodations for a fee unless licensed") because it sets no limit on fees and none of the six categories covers it. The amended text also says a broker may contract with only one side, either the tenant or the landlord. I treated that as part of the same rule. The document does not state any penalty or exemptions.
